newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Reliance commissions new plant.
newsitem.headline: India's Reliance commissions new plant.

text.p: India's Reliance Industries Ltd (RIL) said on Sunday it had commissioned a plant to manufacture 80,000 tonnes of polyester staple fibre (PSF) each year at Hazira in the western state of Gujarat.
"With the commissioning, the total PSF capacity of RIL has increased to 270,000 tonnes per year, making RIL the fifth largest PSF producer in the world," Reliance said in a statement.
This is Reliance's second PSF plant at Hazira, a port on India's west coast. Commissioned last September, the earlier plant has an 80,000 tpa capacity.

Reliance, which recently commissioned a 120,000 tpa capacity polyester filament yarn plant at Hazira, plans to commission a plant to manufacture polyethylene terephthalate (PET) with a capacity of 80,000 tonnes per year, the statement added.
"The total polyester production capacity will nearly treble to about 600,000 tonnes on completion of all polyester capacity additions at Hazira," the statement said.

After the capacity additions are complete, Reliance expects to see its share of domestic production of PSF increase to over 60 percent in the financial year 1997/98 (April-March) from 38 percent in 1995/96, the statement said.
Reliance also expects its market share in PFY to rise to over 40 percent in 1997/98, against 29 percent in 1995/96.
